title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: In July 2023, the Lao Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare finalized a revised pre-departure training manual for migrant workers. It serves as a curriculum for compulsory training to be provided by employment service enterprises to outgoing migrant workers. To increase migrant workers’ access to counselling, legal assistance, information and training on migration and labour rights, and COVID-19 emergency assistance, the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and the Lao Federation of Trade Unions operate six Migrant Worker Resource Centers (MRCs); a new MRC was established in Bolikhamxay in March 2022. Village Focus International also provides direct support services and information to migrant workers. In total, an estimated 14,728 migrant workers (9,337 women) and 138 family members have been able to avail themselves of these services in Lao PDR in 2022-2023. Specific information on safe migration for Lao migrants in the fishing and seafood processing sectors has been disseminated to migrant workers via the six MRCs and linked Job Centres in 18 provinces. Returnee women migrant workers have established informal peer networks in Bokeo, Vientiane, and Savannakhet to discuss their migration experiences and provide assistance to each other, and jointly advocate for their needs and concerns with village authorities. Through the MRCs in Savannakhet and Champasak, 11 village savings and loans associations (VSLAs) have been established for 303 women migrant workers. The VSLAs train migrant workers on financial literacy and savings and facilitate dialogues among its members and their family members on labour migration and workplace violence and harassment. The Lao National Chamber of Commerce and Industry organized the first-ever national Employment Expo in Vientiane in March 2022. The event was attended by 918 workers (516 women) and reached an audience of over 100,000 through virtual meetings and social media platforms. ILO, with support of the Government of Australia, provided suggestions and supported two review workshops and two pilot training to employment service enterprises to allow the Ministry to refine the manuals’ content in 2022-23. ILO, with support of the Government of Australia and the European Union, has been building the capacity of its MRC partners to operate the physical MRC centres. MRC staff have been trained on MRC management, data collection, community outreach, financial and results reporting, as well as developed the skills of the MRC staff to deliver counselling, legal assistance, outreach, information and training on migration, labour rights (including for workers in the fishing and seafood processing sectors), skills’ development, and COVID-19 emergency assistance. ILO provided technical support to the Lao Federation of Trade Unions (LFTU) to finalize and print outreach materials. In response to the need among women migrant workers for financial literacy and savings skills, ILO in partnership with Village Focus International (VFI) and the MRCs in Savannakhet and Champasek provinces, set up VSLAs for migrant workers; MRC staff provide financial literacy training through the training-of-trainers provided by VFI and ILO. ILO supported the Lao National Chamber of Commerce and Industry to organize a National Employment Expo in March 2022 in Vientiane. The Expo provided labour market information and job-matching opportunities for unemployed workers during COVID-19, including return migrant workers.

title.narrative: 7.5.2. Number of Member States with new or improved services to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: The Ministerial Agreement No. 1050 on the Management of Employment Service Enterprises (formerly called “Agreement 043”) was adopted on 25 March 2022. The Agreement includes several articles stating that recruitment-related costs and fees should not be borne by workers. It requires that employment service enterprises cover the cost of most fees associated with the recruitment of migrant workers, including documentation, travel, training, food, and accommodation. It also prohibits these enterprises from charging “workers employment service fees.” This standard can be considered in line with the ILO’s Private Recruitment Agency Convention, 1997 (No. 181). In July 2023, the “Manual for the Management and Protection of migrant workers” of the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare (MOLSW), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry of Public Security was finalized. This manual outlines labour migration-related responsibilities between the three ministries and aims to increase the collaboration between them. MOLSW coordinates the migration network group through which civil society and government stakeholders can engage regularly on violence against women (VAW) and migration issues. It serves as a dialogue network with tripartite partners and recruitment agencies as well. As a result, there has been increased information sharing and coordination between stakeholders. it organizes the dialogue network with tripartite partners and recruitment agencies. The ILO, with the support of the Government of Australia, supported the drafting of Agreement No. 1050 on the Management of Employment Service Enterprises through technical inputs and interventions. The ILO, with the support of the Government of Australia, facilitated and provided inputs for the “Manual for the Management and Protection of migrant workers”. The ILO, with the support of the European Union (EU), worked with the MOLSW to establish the network, and has supported the regular organisation of the network meetings; the third migration network meeting on 15 September 2022 in Vientiane with over 45 participants from relevant government ministries, international organizations, and CSOs. The ILO provided substantive technical comments into the draft regulation in 2022-23 and supported two tripartite consultation meetings.
